claims.text: Overall tribo-corrosion degradation in high-entropy alloys is governed by the interplay between wear-induced passive-film disruption and passive-film regeneration or maintenance.
Rapid re-passivation limits wear damage relative to baseline materials.
Rapid re-passivation limits corrosion damage relative to baseline materials.
Slow or compromised re-passivation produces synergistically accelerated degradation.
The proposed initial alloy is homogeneous and single-phase.
The proposed initial alloy has an intact protective passive film.
Mechanical wear periodically removes the protective oxide film.
Removal of the oxide film exposes fresh, reactive alloy surface.
Rapid oxide-film re-formation mitigates subsequent corrosion.
Inefficient film re-formation allows accelerated electrochemical attack of exposed surfaces.
Accelerated electrochemical attack creates a positive feedback that increases total degradation.
Under conditions permitting rapid passive-film regeneration, the high-entropy alloy will have lower combined wear and corrosion loss than the matched baseline.
When oxide-film re-formation is impaired, total degradation will exceed the additive effects of separately measured wear and corrosion.
The proposed mechanism applies in environments with moderate pH, temperature, and chemical aggressiveness that support oxide-film formation.
The proposed mechanism may fail at very low pH because protective-film formation or stability can be compromised.
The proposed mechanism may fail under excessively high mechanical stress because protective-film formation or stability can be compromised.
Variations in local microstructure may alter tribo-corrosion synergy under different conditions.
